subject: Geo-locks & scheduled erasures: product/engineering sync for Pharmaco
messages:
From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@pharmaco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: data-ops@pharmaco.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Geo-lock requirements and erasure scheduling for PHARMACO (SOW draft)

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed with our legal and cloud teams, we need to firm up two items in the SOW before legal signs:

1) Tenant-level geo-locks: we need the ability to lock a tenant (or workspace) to EU-only storage for all persisted artifacts (request logs, embeddings, model cache snapshots). This must be enforceable via API and visible in the admin UI.

2) Configurable erasure windows: patients data requires a scheduled erasure capability where we can specify a cadence (e.g., 90 days, 365 days) per dataset with a blackout window for backups. We also need an "export before erase" ability and an estimated SLA for the actual erase to hit all replicas (we expect an auditable timestamp).

I've attached a redline of the SOW and a sample erasure schedule CSV. Please confirm whether Redwood can meet these out of the box, or if there are roadmap items or engineering prerequisites we should plan for.

Also: audit logs must contain the delete/erase job id, actor, timestamp, and region of execution. If you have an example event schema, that would help our compliance reviewers.

Appreciate a quick sync — our legal lead is hoping to close the week of July 8.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Lim
Head of Cloud Security, Pharmaco Therapeutics
Attachments: PHARMACO_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), erasure_schedule_example.csv (csv)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-lock requirements and erasure scheduling for PHARMACO (SOW draft)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. We're aligned that these are critical for regulated customers. A few quick clarifying questions for engineering/product so we scope correctly: 

- Geo-locks: do you need hard-enforced rejects for any write that would route outside EU, or is soft-preference with audit acceptable for initial rollout? (we can offer a hard lock only where storage is physically pinned to EU regions)
- Erasure SLA: when you say "auditable timestamp", is the requirement that the erase job completes on all replicas within X hours and that the timestamp on the audit log marks final completion?
- Export-before-erase: should the export be pushed to your S3 (preferred) or do you need a Redwood-hosted temporary export URL?

I'm looping in Karthik (infra/serving) and Marissa (product) to map to the roadmap. We'll propose a minimal compliance MVP and a full feature set with estimated timelines by EOD Monday.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@pharmaco.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-lock requirements and erasure scheduling for PHARMACO (SOW draft)

Naomi / Marissa / Rachel,

Quick engineering read on the asks: overall feasible but with trade-offs and a short implementation runway. High-level notes:

1) Tenant-level geo-locks (hard pin):
- We can implement a tenant attribute that maps to a geozone and enforce at the routing/orchestration layer. This requires: metadata binding for existing tenants, region-aware placement for persisted artifacts, and on-write validation to reject writes that would persist outside the pinned region.
- Complexity: model cache snapshot routing and background snapshot replication currently assume cross-region warm replicas for fast failover. To support hard pins we need a replica-exclusion mode (no cross-region replication) and an admin option to rehydrate from a pinned snapshot during failover.
- Estimated effort: 3 sprints for infra changes + 1 sprint for admin UI and API endpoints (rough).

2) Scheduled erasures + export-before-erase:
- We already have a retention TTL pipeline for generated content, but it is global and not tenant-scoped. We need per-tenant retention policies with scheduled jobs.
- Export: we can add a job hook that dumps data to a configured customer S3 before deletion. That requires credentials management (KMS/HSM) and a secure transfer path.
- Auditability: we'll surface job lifecycle events to the audit log; final-completion timestamps can be emitted once the deletion job has reconciled across all region stores. The reconciliation window depends on replication topology — with hard-pinned tenants it will be simpler.
- Estimated effort: 2 sprints to add per-tenant retention policy plumbing, 2 sprints to add export hooks and credentials flow, 1 sprint for audit schema and UI.

Proposed near-term approach (compliance MVP):
- Offer a "soft geo-preference" toggle (immediate, low effort) + per-tenant retention TTL with export hook (1–2 months).
- Ship audit schema and reporting for erase jobs (1 month).

Longer-term (full hard-pinned tenants + replication mode): 2–3 quarters to fully validate failover behavior, snapshot handling, and carrier-grade SLA guarantees.

I'll create a JIRA ticket with the infra tasks and a tentative milestone plan for PM prioritization. Kicking off a short scoping doc would help lock dates for legal.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-lock requirements and erasure scheduling for PHARMACO (SOW draft)

Rachel — thanks for the clarity and for the SOW redline. We've discussed internally and propose the following next steps so your legal can proceed: 

1) Compliance MVP proposal (target: July 31):
   - Per-tenant retention TTL with export-before-erase to customer S3 (configurable via admin UI and API).
   - Audit events for erase job lifecycle (start, export-success, delete-queued, delete-complete) with final-completion timestamp.
   - Soft geo-preference toggle documented as not a hard enforcement (we'll include the option and timeline for hard pinning as an appendix).

2) Roadmap appendix (for SOW):
   - Hard geo-pinning + replica-exclusion mode: Q4 2028 (subject to QA/failover testing).
   - SLA language: we'll provide an initial SLA for erase completion for the compliance MVP (best-effort within 72 hours) and an enterprise SLA as part of the hard-pinning milestone.

3) Immediate asks for legal:
   - Confirm whether export-to-customer-S3 is acceptable vs. requiring Redwood-hosted export.
   - Confirm acceptable erase-completion window for the MVP (we suggested 72 hours).

Karthik will open JIRA-INF-3421 with the infra tasks and a proposed sprint-level plan; I'll draft the SOW appendix language and push an updated PDF by Thursday.

Naomi / Stephanie — can we block 30 minutes Thursday to review the proposed SOW appendix before I send the redline back to Pharmaco?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
